root_cause.text: In hci_uart_register_dev(), when hci_register_dev() fails, the HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT flag is not cleared before calling hu->proto->close(hu) and setting hu->hdev to NULL, leaving a race window where concurrent UART data reception via hci_uart_tty_receive() can access freed protocol resources.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states: "When hci_register_dev() fails in hci_uart_register_dev() HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT is not cleared before calling hu->proto->close(hu) and setting hu->hdev to NULL. This means incoming UART data will reach the protocol-specific recv handler in hci_uart_tty_receive() after resources are freed." The patch adds `clear_bit(HCI_UART_PROTO_INIT, &hu->flags)` under a write lock to prevent this race.

In hci_uart_tty_receive() (lines 499-512), after checking HCI_UART_PROTO_SET flag, it calls hu->proto->recv() then accesses hu->hdev->stat.byte_rx. There is a race window: after hci_uart_set_proto() calls p->close(hu) on error and before the calling ioctl clears HCI_UART_PROTO_SET, a concurrent receive can pass the flag check, use a closed protocol, and access the freed hdev.
